headline: Hot US core CPI locks in a December Fed hike and lifts the dollar most since September
summary: The dollar index rose about 0.6% to near 102.2, its best day since September, after core CPI rose 0.3% for a third month against a 0.2% forecast and two-year yields jumped about 18bp, making a December Fed hike a near-certainty. The Aussie, pound and franc fell most, while Asian currencies that closed before the data held gains, led by the peso and won.
drivers: Third hot core CPI puts a 50bp Fed hike in play

Headline CPI rose 0.4% and core 0.3% in October, against 0.3% and 0.2% expected, hours after Governor Waller said such a print would justify considering a half-point hike. Futures moved to fully price a December hike with about 10–15% odds of 50bp, and two-year yields rose to about 4.73%.
Weak local data hit the Aussie and loonie

The Aussie fell about 0.9% to near 0.6866 after Westpac consumer sentiment hit a four-year low and RBA December hike odds slid to about 4%. The loonie dropped to 1.4210, its weakest since Oct 15, as BoC minutes showed no hurry for another hike.
Cheaper oil and returning flows lifted Asia before the data

Brent settled at a two-month low near $91.5 on Trump's pause in Iran strikes, so the peso jumped 40 centavos to 62.91 and the won rose 9.6 to 1,337.5 as foreigners bought Korean shares. The Taiwan dollar only edged up to 32.865 as foreign selling ran a ninth day.
view: More bullish for the next 1–2 weeks: a third hot core print leaves the Fed hiking in December while the RBA and BoC sit tight, and a 50bp move is now a live risk. I back the dollar against the Aussie, loonie and euro and fade it only against the yen near Tokyo's 159–160 line. A DXY close below 101.50, or a soft PPI with Fed pushback from Barr or Jefferson, would turn me neutral.
ideas: Hold the long from 1.4080–1.4100 as the BoC waits and the Fed hikes; for 1.4300, stop 1.4080.
Sell 0.6900–0.6920 with the RBA done and the Fed hiking; for 0.6780, stop 0.6970.
Hold the short from 1.1170–1.1190 as the Fed is fully priced to hike; for 1.1050, stop 1.1260.
review: The USD/CAD buy is about 95 pips in favour and the AUD/USD sale about 45, the EUR/USD short is about 10 pips in favour and the USD/JPY short about 30 against, all inside their stops. I close the rupiah long as JISDOR fixed at 18,059, below the 18,060 stop, and keep every range call.

eurusd.note: Down about 0.5% to near 1.1169, giving back Monday's gain after hot US inflation; the short is slightly in favour.
eurusd.why: The dollar did the moving. US core CPI rose 0.3% in October against a 0.2% forecast, the third such print in a row, and two-year Treasury yields jumped about 18bp to near 4.73% as a December Fed hike became all but certain. The euro got little help from ECB chief economist Lane's view that a December hike would be prudent, because the US surprise was fresher and larger.
eurusd.outlook: I keep the short from 1.1170–1.1190 for 1.1050: the Fed is now fully priced to hike and the pair sits below its 200-period average near 1.1227. A close above 1.1260 would end the call.
eurusd.watch: US PPI (Nov 13), Fed's Barr and Jefferson this week, ECB speakers ahead of December, French bond spreads.

view.call: Short from 1.1170–1.1190; Fed fully priced to hike.

gbpusd.note: Down about 0.7% to near 1.3346, after dipping to about 1.3300, its lowest since late October.
gbpusd.why: The dollar did the moving. Fed Governor Waller said a 0.3% core CPI would put a half-point December hike on the table, and the print delivered exactly that, lifting US yields and erasing sterling's Monday gain. With Bank Rate now level with the top of the Fed's range, the pound lost more than the euro as markets looked ahead to Thursday's UK Q3 GDP.
gbpusd.outlook: I keep the 1.3280–1.3480 range: BoE hike pricing supports dips, while a Fed set to hike in December caps rallies. A close below 1.3280 would open 1.3150, the October low.
gbpusd.watch: UK Q3 GDP (Nov 12), BoE speakers, US PPI (Nov 13), Fed speakers.

view.call: 1.3280–1.3480; hawkish BoE vs a hawkish Fed.

audusd.note: Down about 0.9% to near 0.6866, the weakest major, close to Friday's 0.6855 low; the sale is about 45 pips in favour.
audusd.why: Both sides moved. The hot US CPI lifted the dollar, and the Aussie was hit hardest among majors because local data undercut the RBA: Westpac consumer sentiment fell 2.7% to a four-year low of 78.2 and the NAB survey showed weak business conditions. Markets now price only about a 4% chance of a December RBA hike, so the rate gap is turning in the dollar's favour.
audusd.outlook: I keep the sale from 0.6900–0.6920 for 0.6780: the RBA looks done while the Fed is set to hike. A close above 0.6970 would end the call; a break of 0.6855 opens the target.
audusd.watch: Australia jobs data, China activity data, US PPI (Nov 13), AI-stock sentiment.

view.call: Sell 0.6900–0.6920; RBA has peaked, Fed hiking.

usdjpy.note: Up about 0.45% to near 158.69 on the CPI surprise; the short is about 30 pips against, under its 159.40 stop.
usdjpy.why: The dollar did the moving. Higher US two-year yields after the CPI beat widened the rate gap again, and the yen slipped up to about 0.6%. The BoJ's October Summary of Opinions, in which some members called for faster hikes, failed to help, and weak household spending data added to the yen's softness. The pair is now just below its 100-day average near 159.02.
usdjpy.outlook: I keep the short for 156.50, but with less conviction: Tokyo's 159–160 line caps the upside and the BoJ leans toward December. A close above 159.40 would end the call.
usdjpy.watch: US PPI (Nov 13), Japan Q3 GDP, BoJ speakers, Tokyo comments near 159–160.

view.call: Short from 158.20–158.50; Tokyo's 160 line, BoJ hawkish.

usdchf.note: Up about 0.65% to near 0.8249, its best level in about two weeks, as the franc fell with other havens.
usdchf.why: The dollar did the moving. Higher US yields after the CPI beat made the zero-yielding franc less attractive, and calmer markets after Trump played down new strikes on Iran kept haven demand low. Gold fell more than 2% on the same forces, a sign that the US rate story, not Swiss news, set the day.
usdchf.outlook: I keep the 0.8130–0.8280 range: a hawkish Fed lifts the pair, but the franc regains demand on any equity slide. A close above 0.8280 would open 0.8350.
usdchf.watch: US PPI (Nov 13), Swiss inflation, SNB sight deposits, equity sentiment.

usdcad.note: Up about 0.5% to near 1.4188 after touching 1.4210, the loonie's weakest since Oct 15; the buy is about 95 pips in favour.
usdcad.why: Both sides moved. The CPI beat lifted the dollar, while BoC minutes from the October hike gave no sign of a follow-up in December, and economists said lower energy prices remove the urgency. Brent settled down 1.2% at $91.49, a two-month low, after Friday's third straight monthly jobs loss in Canada had already sapped the loonie.
usdcad.outlook: I hold the buy for a higher 1.4300 target and move the stop to 1.4080, about break-even: a Fed hiking while the BoC waits favours the dollar. A close below 1.4080 would end the call.
usdcad.watch: US PPI (Nov 13), Canada inflation, BoC speakers, oil and US-Iran headlines.

view.call: Long from 1.4080–1.4100; Fed hikes, BoC on hold.

usdcnh.note: Little changed near 6.676 offshore after the PBOC set a fixing 512 pips weaker than the Reuters estimate.
usdcnh.why: Beijing did the moving. The PBOC fixed the midpoint at 6.7167, a record 512 pips weaker than the market estimate of 6.6655, a clear signal it wants the yuan's 5% rally to slow. Exporters' year-end dollar sales absorbed that pressure in Asian hours, and the yuan barely reacted to the US CPI beat later, unlike the Aussie or yen.
usdcnh.outlook: I keep the 6.64–6.70 range: the PBOC leans against gains while exporters sell dollars on rallies. A close above 6.70 would show Beijing wants a weaker yuan.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15), China credit and activity data.

view.call: 6.64–6.70; PBOC slows the yuan, exporters sell USD.

usdhkd.note: Little changed near 7.845, still close to the weak end of the 7.75–7.85 band.
usdhkd.why: Nothing local moved the pair. HKMA bill yields eased about 2–5bp at Tuesday's tender to near 2.8–2.9%, while US two-year yields jumped to about 4.73% after the CPI beat, widening the carry gap that favours holding US dollars. That keeps the Hong Kong dollar parked near the weak side of its peg.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: the carry gap keeps it near 7.85, and only a jump in HIBOR or HKMA buying at 7.85 would pull it lower.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA operations at 7.85, HIBOR, US PPI (Nov 13).

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Up about 0.3% to near 1.2822 as the dollar rallied on US inflation after Singapore's close.
usdsgd.why: The dollar did the moving. The Singapore dollar was steady in Asian hours as oil slid and regional stocks rallied, then lost ground in New York when the CPI beat lifted US yields. It fell less than the Aussie or pound because the MAS policy band, which keeps the currency on a gradual appreciating path, limits swings.
usdsgd.outlook: I keep the 1.2740–1.2860 range: the MAS band supports the currency, but a Fed set to hike limits gains. A close above 1.2860 would open 1.2920.
usdsgd.watch: US PPI (Nov 13), Singapore final Q3 GDP, Asian tech-stock flows.

usdkrw.note: Won rose 9.6 to 1,337.5 in Seoul, a two-session gain of 19.1; it eased to about 1,342 offshore after US CPI.
usdkrw.why: The won did the moving in Seoul. The Kospi jumped 4.4% to 5,239 on a tech rebound and cheaper oil, and foreigners turned net buyers of about 350bn won of shares after seven straight days of selling. Exporters added dollar sales, pushing the pair to an intraday low of 1,335.1, before the US CPI beat trimmed the gain in offshore trade.
usdkrw.outlook: I keep the 1,330–1,365 range: foreign buying has returned, but a Fed set to hike limits the won's gains. A Seoul close below 1,330 would open 1,315; above 1,365 would revive the long.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows, Korean authorities' comments, AI-chip sentiment, US PPI (Nov 13).

view.call: 1,330–1,365; foreign buying returns vs firm Fed.

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar edged up 1.7 cents to 32.865 in Taipei after hitting 32.97; offshore near 32.94 after US CPI.
usdtwd.why: Foreign outflows and the central bank did the moving. The Taiex rose about 2.5% on state-fund buying and short-selling limits, yet foreigners sold about NT$34bn of shares, a ninth straight day and over NT$800bn in total, pushing the currency close to 33. Exporters sold dollars above 32.9 and the central bank stepped in late; its governor said November's roughly US$10bn of outflows was portfolio reallocation, not a run.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep the 32.60–33.05 range: officials defend 33, while foreign selling is slowing but not yet reversing. A close above 33.05 would show the defence has failed.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, stabilisation fund buying, central bank action, US PPI (Nov 13).

usdmyr.note: Ringgit edged up to 4.0540/0580 at the 6pm KL close, from 4.0565/0610 before the Deepavali holiday.
usdmyr.why: The dollar did the moving, gently. Back from the holiday, the ringgit traded between 4.0510 and 4.0590, helped by the dollar's pullback in Asian hours and hopes of a US-Iran de-escalation. Gains were small because Brent's slide toward $90 trims Malaysia's oil and gas income, and the hot US CPI came after the local close.
usdmyr.outlook: I keep the 4.035–4.085 range: Bank Negara's steady 2.75% rate supports the ringgit, but a Fed set to hike limits gains.
usdmyr.watch: Malaysia Q3 GDP and trade data, regional chip stocks, US PPI (Nov 13).

usdphp.note: Peso jumped 40 centavos to 62.91 at the BAP close, its strongest finish since Oct 14.
usdphp.why: The peso did the moving. Cheaper oil is the peso's biggest swing factor, and Brent's slide to a two-month low eases the Philippines' import bill and inflation, alongside local fuel price cuts that took effect on Tuesday. Volume rose to $1.83bn from $1.26bn as the peso recovered Monday's GDP-driven loss; the US CPI beat came after Manila had closed.
usdphp.outlook: I keep the 62.70–63.50 range, now neutral within it: cheaper oil and remittance season help, but weak growth and a hiking Fed limit gains. A close below 62.70 would open 62.40.
usdphp.watch: BSP comments after the GDP miss, oil, US PPI (Nov 13), BSP decision (Dec 17).

usdidr.note: Rupiah firmed 23 points to 18,062; Bank Indonesia's JISDOR fell to 18,059, under the 18,060 stop.
usdidr.why: The rupiah did the moving in Jakarta. Trump's pause on new strikes against Iran and cheaper oil lifted Asian currencies, and the rupiah rose for a second day to an intraday best near 18,030. Gains stayed modest because September retail sales slowed to 0.6% growth and investors are waiting for the MSCI index review this week; the US CPI beat came after the close.
usdidr.outlook: I close the long at the 18,060 stop and move to an 18,000–18,200 range: a hiking Fed and MSCI risk weigh on the rupiah, but cheaper oil helps. A close above 18,200 would revive the long.
usdidr.watch: MSCI index review (Nov 11–12), Bank Indonesia operations, US PPI (Nov 13), foreign bond flows.

usdinr.note: No onshore trade: India was shut for Diwali-Balipratipada; Monday's close was 93.9275.
usdinr.why: Nothing local moved the rupee because Indian markets were closed for the holiday. Offshore, the backdrop was mixed: Brent's slide to about $91.5 is a strong positive for India's import bill, but the US CPI beat and the jump in US yields lifted the dollar across Asia after hours, which may weigh on the rupee when trading resumes on Wednesday.
usdinr.outlook: I keep the 93.50–94.50 range: oil and inflows favour the rupee, but RBI dollar buying caps gains. A Brent close back above $105 would push it toward 94.50.
usdinr.watch: Market reopening (Nov 11), oil and US-Iran headlines, RBI dollar buying, India inflation data.

view.call: 93.50–94.50; oil and inflows vs RBI buying.

eurjpy.note: Little changed near 177.2, mid-range, as the euro and yen fell by similar amounts against the dollar.
eurjpy.why: Neither side moved much. The US CPI beat pushed both the euro and yen down roughly 0.5% against the dollar, so the cross held near Monday's level. A hawkish ECB, with Lane open to a December hike, offset the BoJ minutes that also leaned toward tightening.
eurjpy.outlook: I keep the 175.5–178.0 range: a hawkish BoJ caps rallies, while Japan's fiscal worries limit dips. A close above 178.0 would open 179.
eurjpy.watch: Tokyo comments, Japan Q3 GDP, ECB speakers, equity sentiment.

cnhjpy.note: Up about 0.4% to near 23.77 as the yen fell on US yields and the yuan held steady.
cnhjpy.why: The yen did the moving. It weakened against the dollar after the CPI beat lifted US yields, while the yuan barely moved because exporters' dollar sales offset a much weaker PBOC fixing. That pushed the cross toward the top of its range.
cnhjpy.outlook: I keep the 23.3–23.9 range: Beijing is slowing the yuan and the BoJ leans hawkish, so neither leg should run far. A close above 23.9 would open 24.2.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15), Japan Q3 GDP, Tokyo comments.

watch: Next: Fed's Barr and Jefferson this week, UK Q3 GDP (Nov 12), US PPI (Nov 13), the MSCI review (Nov 11–12), the PBOC's FX reserve hike (Nov 15) and the Fed (Dec 8–9) and BoJ in December, plus Tokyo's 159–160 line, Taiwan's defence of 33 and foreign flows in Asian chip stocks.
